qualitative_or_quantitative_description.value: Under plastic deformation the interaction between κ-carbides and dislocations does not change the plane slip mode, but additional dislocation sources are activated and acted upon by cross slip; nano κ-carbides uniformly distributed in austenite promote plane slip, and as strain increases the plane dislocation structure is further refined, contributing to continuous strain hardening.

interaction_type.value: dislocation pile-up at B2/γ phase boundary

qualitative_or_quantitative_description.value: Compared with κ-carbide, B2 phase is not sheared by slip dislocations, leading to dislocation pile-up at the phase boundary and enhancing work hardening during plastic deformation.

interface_notes.value: The κ'-carbide nucleated within the austenite matrix is ultrafine and shows a coherent relationship with the matrix. The κ-carbide/austenite interface (with vacancies) is considered an effective hydrogen capture center.

phase_evolution.value: When the aging temperature ranges from 500 to 700 °C, spinodal decomposition occurs in austenite: γ → γ' + γ'' → γ'' + L1₂ (short-range ordering phase) + γ' + κ'. At higher aging temperature (700–900 °C) coarse κ'-carbide forms in the austenite matrix or along the prior austenite grain boundary (called intercrystalline κ*-carbide).

slip_behavior.value: In single austenite-base steels, plane slip of dislocations and the shear effect of mobile dislocations on ordered phases dominate; deformation mechanisms (MBIP, DSBR, SIP, TL) depend on stacking fault energy.

source.reason: Describes coherency of κ'-carbide with austenite, the spinodal-decomposition phase evolution during aging, κ-carbide/dislocation and B2/γ interactions, and the κ-carbide/austenite interface role in hydrogen trapping for single austenite-base Fe-Mn-Al-C steels.

processing_steps_notes.value: Hot-rolled to 2–5 mm thickness between 1100 and 850 °C; in some cases reheating between rolling passes is needed to avoid crack generation. A large rolling reduction provides enough recrystallization driving force, inhibiting Fe-Al or FeAl segregation. For austenite-base steels the thermal-mechanical processing temperature is generally located within the single austenite phase region.

unmapped_findings: For austenite-base Fe-Mn-Al-C steel, 1 wt% C contributes a yield-strength increment of 187–300 MPa, whereas 1 wt% Al contributes slightly below 10 MPa; Mn addition improves the austenite fraction and increases the solubility of Al and C in austenite, indirectly affecting mechanical properties. High C (>0.7 wt%) and Al (>7.0 wt%) contents are the primary conditions for κ-carbide formation in single austenite-base Fe-Mn-Al-C steels; the aging temperature and time should be precisely regulated to avoid intergranular κ*-carbide and β-Mn formation. (b0071)

Representative single-austenite Fe-Mn-Al-C SFE / deformation-mechanism data (Table 3): Fe-27Mn-11.5Al-0.95C, SFE 80 mJ·m⁻², DSBR+MBIP, YS/UTS 0.85; Fe-16Mn-2Al-0.45C, SFE 92 mJ·m⁻², TWIP+DSBR, YS/UTS 0.85; Fe-27Mn-12Al-0.9C, SFE 110 mJ·m⁻², DSBR+MBIP, YS/UTS 0.87; Fe-18Mn-7Al-0.85C, SFE 120 mJ·m⁻², DSBR+SIP+MBIP, YS/UTS 0.66. (b0096)

Low-density TWIP steels (single austenite) have a high Mn content of 20–30 wt%; after rolling, annealing and quenching the microstructure consists of complete austenite together with a large number of annealing twins. (b0090)

Fe-28Mn-10Al-1.2C steel with SFE of 110 mJ/m² contains austenite, ferrite and κ-carbides; deformation twins are almost restrained and nano κ-carbides are uniformly arranged on the austenitic matrix with a certain spacing, giving the SIP effect. (b0089)

The MBIP mechanism was proposed for quenched Fe-28Mn-xAl-(0.8–1.0)C steel: nano short-range ordering phases precipitate in partial areas, microbands form under high strain, and the interaction among microbands refines grains (873 MPa tensile strength and 100% total elongation via dynamic Hall-Petch effect). (b0091)
Fe-30.4Mn-8Al-1.2C low-density steel with SFE of 85 mJ/m² deforms mainly by dynamic slip band refinement (DSBR), giving 900 MPa tensile strength and 68% total elongation. (b0091)
